messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-9876 — high 5xx rate detected for embeddings-service-prod. Trigger: error-rate > 2% for 1m. See https://pagerduty.example/PD-9876
ashley: acked and taking. hopping on it now.
ashley: quick check — dashboard shows a 3.4% 5xx spike starting at ~3897654250, tailing off a bit.
mohit: i'm looking at router logs, seeing a handful of timeouts downstream to kv-cache instances — latency on kv-cache up to 250ms briefly.
tess: @ashley any customer-facing incidents reported? support queue looks quiet so far, no elevated error reports.
ashley: no customer tickets yet, but rolling alerting pages hunting. could be cold kv-cache warming or brief GC.
pagerduty-bot: PD-9876 assigned to ashley. Escalation timer set (5m).
ashley: running a quick grep on logs:
```
grep "timeout" /var/log/embeddings/requests.log | head -n 40
# most timeouts show kv-cache connection reset and transient 503s
```
sam: can we try soft-restart the kv-cache pool on the 3 nodes that show high RT? i'd prefer drain+restart if it helps.
maria: I'm running `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache --namespace=prod --field-selector=metadata.name in (kv-cache-2,kv-cache-7,kv-cache-9)` to cycle the hot pods one at a time.
ops-bot: Started restart of kv-cache-7 (pod kv-cache-7) — will wait for readiness.
ashley: noted. rerouting should be automatic. i'm increasing ingress timeout threshold temporarily to avoid client-side 5xx.
mohit: metrics responding — kv-cache latency back down to ~20ms on rotated pods. 5xx rate dropping in the embeddings service.
incident-bot: PD-9876 auto-resolved after 2m 28s (condition cleared).
ashley: confirmed downstream error rate back to baseline. no customer impact observed.
tess: thanks. This looks like a transient flappy issue during a brief node GC or kernel OOM? any logs indicating OOM killer?
maria: node metrics don't show OOM; cpu spike looks small. more likely a transient network hiccup between AZs that affected a subset of kv-cache pods.
sam: since PD auto-resolved, do we still want to create a postmortem or treat as noise? suggestion: create a short RCA note and tighten alerting: require sustained 2m->5m window before paging.
mohit: agree on adjusting alerting threshold. also add a KV warmup health-check in the embeddings path to fail fast to cache-miss rather than cascade 5xx.
ashley: i'll create a quick follow-up ticket and assign. Notes: 1) incident auto-resolved, transient kv-cache latency spike, 2) no customer-facing errors reported, 3) mitigation: rotated affected kv-cache pods, 4) next steps: adjust alerting window + add warmup health-check + runbook entry for soft-restart.
incident-bot: PD-9876 closed (auto-resolve).
ashley: tagging @oncall-rota and SRE to review runbook. closing thread, but will attach logs to the ticket: https://tickets.example/RED-3421
maria: adding a short blameless note to RED-3421 now.
sam: thanks all. small noisy pocket, worth tuning alerts so we don't get flapping pages. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled noise-suppression tweak has been proposed in infra-alerts; linking to PR #483.
ashley: +1 — will follow up in the PR and drop the quick runbook snippet there.
